quotes.text: Keeping data local isn't always about distrust of the cloud. Sometimes it's about law, sometimes about speed, and sometimes about keeping the business running when the network fails.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the three real reasons workloads stay on premises.

quotes.text: Azure local doesn't copy all of public Azure into a rack of servers. You don't suddenly get every Azure service running locally just because you installed Azure local.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Corrects the common 'Azure in a box' misconception.

quotes.text: Azure Arc is the management layer. It can connect many kinds of existing infrastructure to Azure, including systems that aren't Azure local at all.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clearly separates Azure Arc from Azure Local.

quotes.text: The goal isn't to put everything local. The goal is to put each workload in the place where it can do its job properly.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A balanced decision rule for hybrid workload placement.

quotes.text: Here's the thing, if a factory stops working when the internet drops, a cloud-only design has already put that workload in the wrong place.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable test for whether a workload needs local infrastructure.

takeaways: Azure Local runs virtual machines, containers and selected Azure services on validated hardware at your own site, while Azure provides management, monitoring, policy and security.
Azure Arc is the management layer that connects any outside infrastructure to Azure, whereas Azure Local is the hyperconverged platform where local workloads actually run.
Choose Azure Local when latency, data location rules, required offline operation or direct control demand it, and start every decision with the workload rather than the hardware.
hook: Some workloads cannot leave the factory, hospital or store, yet running them on isolated local servers splits teams and tools. This Simply Explained episode helps IT pros and architects understand what Azure Local is, how it differs from Azure Arc, and when bringing Azure management to on-premises workloads really makes sense.
